w: Swamishri addressed a small assembly of tribal people. The weekly Satsang assembly at Jamalapada is attended by 20 - 25 tribal men and women devotees.

After Thakorji's darshan at 7.45 am Swamishri joined the De-addiction Rally by children who were to join the 20-day anti-addiction campaign. Holding a cardboard banner saying, 'Renounce Addiction, Worship God', Swamishri encouraged the children by joining the small rally from the mandir steps to the assembly hall.

At 10.35 am Swamishri performed the foundation stone laying ceremony for 'Pramukh Swami General Hospital'. The BAPS Sanstha's 6 storey, modern hospital planned to be completed in the next three years will be a blessing to the people of Surat. During his blessings Swamishri pointed out, "Any person who follows the commands prescribed by the scriptures is happy. Because of a lack in self-control or abstinence, hospitals are made, doctors are trained and medicines are invented. But if man exercises self control and obedience to the scriptural commands then he will be safe from disease and will thus become happy…"

At 2 p.m., a grand symbolic Rath Yatra under the auspices of BAPS Golden Anniversary of Children’s Activities was launched from Alperton High School in London. About 6,000 devotees from London, Leicester, Birmingham and other cities participated in the devotional event. Children and youth colorfully dressed for the occasion danced and expressed their devotion and joy in the streets of northwest London. The murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Lord Jagannath were installed in two decorated floats. The disciplined procession resonated with the singing of dhun by the devotees. The Rath Yatra concluded at 5.30 p.m. Then on the mandir grounds Swamishri and the dignitaries, Mayor of Brent Peter Lemmon, Minister of Transport and Aviation Tony Macnulty, M.P. Barry Gardiner, Chairman of Metropolitan Police Authorities Toby Harris and Mayor of London Ken Livingstone released peace pigeons in the air. Children released peace balloons to commemorate the Rath Yatra event. Thereafter a celebration assembly was held in the mandir hall. Mayor of Brent Peter Lemmon said, “The community here is giving a message of peace to the larger community through their activities. Brent is the largest multi-faith community…” Minister for Transport and Aviation Tony Macnulty said, “I was very happy to be part of this Rath Yatra. It is a very joyous day. Wonderful procession for the whole community of London.”

The M.P. I know yet more temples will be opened by His Holiness in Houston and Chicago. It is the same breath that will give life to the murtis there. The same simplicity and holiness in the murti will give life to the community there as it gives life here.” The chairman of the Metropolitan Police Authority Lord Toby Harris said, “Young people are inspired to work for the community, that is a powerful message to all the communities of London.”

The Mayer of London Ken Livingstone said, “Your Holiness, we met 20 years ago in Alexandra Palace. I had no idea then about the beauty of the building you would create in this city. It has impounded this city with its beauty, and increased the beauty of this city beyond measure. I praise you for the work you’ve done for this city and for peace and for the children whose 50th anniversary we will shortly celebrate.” Finally Swamishri crowned the assembly with his blessings, “Today’s festival was celebrated beautifully. Everyone participated by chanting God’s holy name. By celebrating such festivals our spiritual strength, devotion and remembrance of God increases.”

Swamishri was absorbed in reading a letter. At that time a little boy called Hari entered. He went upto Swamishri and said, “Swami, I’d like to tell you a story.” Though the boy was disturbing Swamishri’s work, Swamishri did not displease him. “Why one, tell me two,” Swamishri replied. Then Swamishri placed his spectacles and the letter on one side and gave his undivided attention to the boy. Hari could just about manage to talk in Gujarati. The only two Gujarati words that could be understood in his story were ‘Bhagatji Maharaj’ and ‘churma’ (sweetened baked flour). Hari narrated the incident of Bhagatji Maharaj eating the baked flour in his childhood.

Swamishri understood the story from two words spoken by the boy. Swamishri listened to Hari’s story with rapt attention till he finished speaking. Then Swamishri called him closer and remarked that he should also do likewise and then hide away. Swamishri’s love and patience encouraged the child and made him happy.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was absorbed in reading letters, and just then a child named Hari came to Swamishri. He said to Swamishri, who was reading a letter, "Bapa! I want to tell you one thing."

"Why one, tell me two!" For Swamishri, who was reading letters, this child was really an interruption, but Swamishri did not disappoint him. He immediately joined in his talk. To listen to him, Swamishri took off his glasses. He put the letter to one side and began to listen attentively. Hari could barely speak Gujarati. If there was one word that could be heard clearly in his English-tinged Gujarati, it was "Bhagatji Maharaj". Hari told Swamishri, as well and as much as he knew it, the story "Bhagatji Maharaj ate the churmu (a sweet)".

Swamishri too kept listening attentively to the churmu story. Because of the two words "churmu" and "Bhagatji Maharaj", Swamishri could follow the whole story, and even so Swamishri listened attentively to Hari's whole story.
Hari finished the story. Swamishri called him close. Laughing, blessing him and joking, he said, "Hari! You should do that at home, and then go and hide."
Swamishri's art of encouraging children by giving them love and warmth in this way, and turning them towards satsang, is wonderful.

At 10:30 am Swamishri departed for the suburb of Maninagar. Here, at the newly constructed BAPS Swaminarayan mandir Swamishri consecrated the charanarvind (footprints) of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Thereafter he performed the pujan and arti rituals of the murtis. In his blessings to the assembly Swamishri said, “Shriji Maharaj and sadhus have been to Maninagar so this place is a holy place. Due to the efforts of sadhus the Satsang has grown here so we were inspired to create a mandir here for the benefit of society…”

An editor of a Gujarati daily came for Swamishri’s darshan and blessings. With reference to the present media world Swamishri advised, “There is a proverb which says ‘Shabde maryã mari gayã... Sharp words kill and at the utterance of a word people have left their kingdoms. Those who reflect upon words their mission is fulfilled.’ Draupadi only uttered one sentence, ‘To the blind are born the blind!’ And because of this the Mahabharat war occured.

“Tulsidas thought upon the words of his wife who said, ‘Jesi prit harãmse... The love for the body is useless, such love one should have for God. Go to Vaikunth where no one can catch you.’ By reflecting upon these words he became free of bad traits and became a great sage. King Gopichand was exhorted by his mother, ‘Your golden body will turn into ash.’ Gopichand pondered upon these words and he renounced his kingdom. King Rishabdev preached to his 100 sons and they all renounced the royal pleasures. Out of them Bharatji was king, but he, too, left his kingship. So the words one writes and speaks should be written after great thought.
“If words are not used properly then they create commotion, and if used appropriately they inspire.”
The editor responded, “I, too, must use words after due thought.”

“When you call a blind man ‘Heh, blind one,’ then he will not like it even though he is blind. But by calling him ‘Surdasji’ he becomes happy. Similarly, by exercising vivek (respect) it will have a positive impact. When one twists the news it causes unrest and turmoil in society, whereas good news brings peace.”

At 9.15 am Swamishri presided over the Aksharbrahma Yagna for World Peace. Swamishri performed the pujan and arti rituals of the murtis for the BAPS mandir, Junagadh and murtis for six hari mandirs, namely, Majra, Keshod, Mendarda, Swamina Bodka, Moti Maarad, Bhayavadar. From 3.30 pm to 6.15 pm a grand procession of the murtis was carried out in the city.
In the evening, part two of Jai Jai Gunatitanand was enacted.

A mahapuja was arranged for the foundation-stone laying ceremony of a shikharbaddh mandir in Selvas. More than 350 devotees had come to participate from Selvas to Bochasan. The mahapuja rituals were performed in the presence of senior sadhus and devotees. Swamishri performed pujan of soil brought from Selvas and showered rose petals on and performed pujan of the foundation shilas. Finally Swamishri performed arti and blessed the devotees of Selvas. At 11.25 am Swamishri blessed the Punam assembly, “One’s human birth is fulfilled when one understands the form of God. When the understanding that one is atma, which is our true form, is confirmed, then the bonds of maya and infatuation are dissolved. Thereafter one attains the divine abode of God. The Satpurush’s greatest service is to redeem us from ignorance, maya and base instincts and bless us with a God-conscious life. This is the wealth he gives us. He does not have any other wealth other than God.”

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
25 April 2007, Bochasan
Five hundred devotees pilgrimaged from the towns and villages of Anand, Vidyanagar, Karamsad, Jitodiya and others.

Swamishri departed from Bochasan or at 5.10 pm and arrived in Ahmedabad at 6.45 pm. After a home visit, Swamishri arrived at Amdavad mandir for darshan. Swamishri blessed the large gathering of devotees before departing to Gandhinagar.

Shri Dipakbhai, a devoted bhakta and diamond merchant from Nanivavdi (now in Surat), had passed away suddenly. Shaken by this, his father, brothers and family members had come to seek consolation. When Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave his blessings, the father, choked with emotion, said, "Why did this happen so untimely?"

Swamishri said, "It is a human body. From the moment of birth, its death is certain. The cause can be different. Someone drowns in water, someone dies in war, someone dies of illness. But one who is a devotee of God always attains a good destiny. So do not worry at all that because it was an untimely death he will have a bad fate. He was a devotee, so he has gone to Akshardham. Dipakbhai accomplished great work in a few days, and his bond of debt with you was complete, so God took him."

ds.t: Peace only when one's nature changes
w: There was a letter from a woman abroad. She had written: "My husband's heart valve surgery went well, but for a long time now he has not been coming to the mandir and he sees faults in the devotees. I myself also serve as a volunteer, but I too see faults. There are also many quarrels at home. We quarrel, finding fault with each other. Please be compassionate now. In fits of anger I treat my own children like animals. When my husband and I get angry, we lose control of our words. Please make it so that we do not get angry."

Replying to the letter, Pramukh Swami Maharaj dictated: "Only when one's nature changes will there be peace. Write to her that when anger comes, she should do bhajan, 'Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan...', and one of the two should leave the place."

Today Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the Sunday assembly. In today's assembly the kishore mandal gave a beautiful presentation. At the end of the assembly, Ishwarcharan Swami offered Swamishri a kalash (pot) made by the kishore and kishori mandals of Dholka, filled with notes of niyams. Swamishri himself took in his hands this kalash, full of inner wealth and expressing commitment to walk the path of niyams, showed it to everyone all around and said, "This has not been filled with rupees, it has been filled with notes of niyam and dharma." Saying this, he himself opened the kalash, put his hand inside, took out the notes, showed them to everyone and said, "Keep niyam and dharma firm like this."

Today Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the Sunday assembly. In today's assembly the teenagers' group made a beautiful presentation. At the end of the assembly, Ishwarcharan Swami offered Swamishri a kalash (pot) made by the teenage boys' and girls' groups of Dholka, containing slips of paper with niyams. Swamishri himself took in his hands this kalash, full of inner wealth and expressing their commitment to walk the path of niyams, showed it to everyone on all sides and said, "This has not been filled with rupees, it has been filled with slips of niyams and dharma." Saying this, he himself opened the kalash, put his hand inside, took out the slips and showed them to everyone, and said, "Keep your niyams and dharma firm like this."

ds.t: Nanda's cap was back to front
w: When Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his meal, since today was the patotsav (anniversary) of the Ahmedabad mandir, Hrishikeshdas Swami had found the description of the pratishtha in the biography of Yogiji Maharaj and read it out.
Swamishri smiled and said, "At that time Nanda Saheb was wearing his cap back to front. His wife had someone tell him, and then he put it on straight!"
What an amazing memory Swamishri has! One might remember the main events of the pratishtha, but to remember after 55 years that Nandaji's cap was back to front?
